rows.opening: Mercury in Aquarius makes the odd idea sound more useful than the familiar answer. After moving through {{priorSign}} from {{priorSignEntryDate}} to {{priorSignExitDate}}, Mercury enters Aquarius on {{entryDate}}, and our attention shifts toward patterns, future possibilities, and unusual solutions. A question opens a new route through a stuck conversation. Notes that seemed unrelated form a clear pattern. A strange suggestion becomes the first answer that fits.
rows.tension: The speed of that insight creates distance when everyone else is still catching up. We skip the explanation, point out the flaw, and move straight to a solution that feels obvious to us. If someone hesitates, we may argue harder or take the opposite side just to keep the thinking alive. The idea gets more interesting, but the exchange gets colder. What began as a useful break from convention ends with the person hearing it feeling treated like part of the problem.
rows.development: Mercury last moved through Aquarius from {{previousResidencyEntryDate}} to {{previousResidencyExitDate}}. Now a group discussion can start chasing the most original take instead of the useful one. A writer can keep refining the theory while missing the sentence that would make it clear. We can spot the system behind a recurring problem and still lose trust by treating every objection as outdated. When every answer has to sound original, useful questions go unsaid. Decisions then rest on a clever pattern that nobody had enough time to examine.
rows.close: Before {{exitDate}}, the strongest idea may still go nowhere once questioning it feels like admitting we cannot keep up.

We can try the unusual fix on something low-stakes and write down what changed.

rows.opening: Mars enters Taurus on {{entryDate}} after moving through {{priorSign}} from {{priorSignEntryDate}} to {{priorSignExitDate}}, and action becomes slower but much harder to stop. A task that resisted a quick fix gets another careful pass. A heavy load moves one trip at a time. Once the goal feels worth the effort, we can keep going long after the first burst of motivation would have faded.
rows.tension: That persistence costs us when changing course starts to feel like surrender. We keep using the same approach after it stops helping, because changing it would expose how much effort went nowhere. Refusal can stay quiet. We say yes to a plan, then move so slowly that nothing changes. Frustration builds until a small obstacle gets treated like a challenge that must be beaten.
rows.development: Mars last moved through Taurus from {{previousResidencyEntryDate}} to {{previousResidencyExitDate}}. The same stubborn effort can show up again now. A stuck repair gets more force instead of a different tool. A familiar routine continues even when it no longer produces the result. In a disagreement, we repeat the same point with more pressure and call that patience. Energy that could move the goal forward goes into defending the first method. By the time anger is obvious, the delay is no longer coming from a lack of strength. It comes from spending that strength against any change in direction.
rows.close: By {{exitDate}}, some goals may be unfinished not because effort was missing, but because too much of it went into proving the first way should have worked.

We can retry one stalled task with a different tool instead of adding more force.
We can finish one small physical job this week, such as tightening a loose handle or moving a box that has been sitting in the way.

rows.opening: After moving through {{priorSign}} from {{priorSignEntryDate}} to {{priorSignExitDate}}, Mars enters Cancer on {{entryDate}}, and protecting what matters starts to outrank moving fast. We notice the strain in someone’s voice and step in. We wait until a choice feels safe before acting. Once we commit, we put deep emotional energy behind the choice.
rows.tension: The trouble starts when protection moves faster than honesty. We feel hurt, decide something is unsafe, and act before admitting why. A simple question gets a defensive answer. We help without being asked, then treat the lack of thanks as proof that care is not returned. The anger moves sideways, so everyone reacts to the tone while the original hurt remains unnamed.
rows.development: Mars last moved through Cancer from {{previousResidencyEntryDate}} to {{previousResidencyExitDate}}. The same pattern can return in small moments that seem unrelated. We handle what someone forgot and grow cold because the effort went unnoticed. We change the subject to hide how much something hurt, then hear the next harmless comment as another threat. Directness feels risky because naming the hurt would show how much it mattered. Indirect action feels safer, but it gives everyone the reaction and withholds the reason. Care then gets mixed with control: checking in becomes checking up, helping becomes taking over, and silence becomes a way to make displeasure felt. By then, the original need is buried under a conflict that cannot be solved clearly.
rows.close: Before {{exitDate}}, the conflict keeps growing when everyone can see the defense and no one knows what it is defending.
try_this: We can take a brisk twenty-minute walk after a defensive reaction instead of carrying the heat into the next exchange.
We can ask whether help is wanted before taking over something someone else is handling.
We can name one hurt in a single plain sentence before it turns into a sharp answer about something else.

We make a bigger show of the effort, claim more credit, or turn the first objection into a fight. The work starts serving the need to prove we matter. Being seen takes over from doing something worth respecting.

rows.opening: Mars in Virgo makes every loose screw, skipped step, and unfinished repair harder to ignore. After moving through {{priorSign}} from {{priorSignEntryDate}} to {{priorSignExitDate}}, Mars enters Virgo on {{entryDate}}, and action shifts toward precision, repair, and practical results. The crooked shelf gets leveled. The repeated mistake gets traced to its source. A vague intention becomes a sequence we can actually follow. This transit wants effort to produce a visible improvement, not just more motion.
rows.tension: That sharp eye rarely stops with the first useful correction. We redo work that already functions, interrupt someone's method to point out a cleaner one, and spend an hour on a flaw that changes almost nothing. Anxiety rises because there is always another detail available to manage. Criticism follows, first as a way to improve the result and then as a running account of everything still wrong. The priority waits while our energy is burned on control.
rows.development: Mars last moved through Virgo from {{previousResidencyEntryDate}} to {{previousResidencyExitDate}}. Similar pressure may return through the habits it leaves behind: checking again after the answer is clear, taking over a small task because explaining it seems inefficient, or treating fatigue as evidence that the routine needs one more adjustment. Each correction offers a quick sense of relief. Together they create more work, and the larger problem stays intact. The method becomes so exact that nobody else can easily join in. Help arrives and gets corrected. A finished result is reopened for one minor change. What began as practical action becomes an exhausting effort to prevent any mistake at all.
rows.close: Before {{exitDate}}, the smallest flaws can be corrected while the priority that started all this is still waiting.
try_this: We can fix one broken or unreliable item and stop as soon as it works.
We can do one necessary cleanup and leave the cosmetic flaws alone.
